content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Is there a way to record the date and time when an event occurs? I want to monitor an event and log its on/off times, then show the event history on the [product_name] display. Thanks in advance!

Hi, The answer depends on how many events you need to save and how long you want to keep that history. It would help to have a bit more detail on your requirements. A simple method is linking a message to the event and showing the enable time and date, making it visible when the message activates. If you require extensive historical data, things get more complicated, and we’d need more information. Alternatively, you could use Excel and a PC to log data. There’s an interesting discussion on this approach in the German forum: Excel logo logger.

Hello, I'm trying to keep track of a gas burner turning on and off so I can estimate gas usage. Generally, the burner switches about 3 to 4 times daily, so a log of 20 events would cover a week, which works for me. I have a program now following your suggestion that logs the date, time, and duration. However, the setup has become quite complicated. My issue is updating each log entry when the burner cycles without losing previous data. I’m currently using the simulator; I didn’t realize you could browse message history directly from the [product_name] display buttons. Right now, I use a reset button to review logs, but that deletes the data each time. I’ve attached my program—any advice on improving its organization would be appreciated.

Hello [user_name], I checked your program to see how I could help. I created a smaller sample program (with 5 log screens) that does the same function with fewer blocks—open it up to take a look. The main difference is that you can't reset logs or screens while the burner is running, but you can modify it if that feature is needed. You can expand the logs further; I think it supports up to about 39 entries. Hope this helps!

[user_name], Try the attached data logger. This is a revised version from the German forum, which I've translated and added some features to. It's an Excel file, so make sure to enable macros in Excel.

analysis.insight_summary: Users want dependable event timestamp logging using [company_name] equipment so they can monitor history and review operational patterns. They struggle with limited log storage, handling overflow, and maintaining prior logs, often making their programs overly complex. To overcome these limitations, some opt for external solutions like Excel for data logging.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [company_name] system to reliably store at least 20 on/off event histories with precise timestamps and to easily review these via the device interface, without accidental data loss.
